title: In-scene UI panel — "Mimetic Controls" synthesizer aesthetic
summary: A bottom-of-screen HUD panel present in every scene (all scenes deliberately share one standardized aspect ratio to support this), with separate GM and player variants, styled after a 1960s-70s synthesizer control panel — knobs, sliders, buttons in a tactile/analog register. Hosts audio-mix sliders and other campaign-management controls.
description:
A custom UI panel, built as procedurally-generated HTML/CSS, living at the bottom of every scene. Feasible specifically because scenes are being deliberately authored at one consistent width/aspect ratio to give the panel a stable place to live. Two variants: a GM version carrying campaign-organization controls and key running-the-scene information, and a player version optimized for what players specifically need to see.

Aesthetic direction, stated explicitly: 'Mimetic Controls' style, modeled on a 1960s-1970s synthesizer — attractive, simple, with room for a lot of well-designed knobs/buttons/sliders rather than flat modern minimalism. This is a specific, deliberate visual identity, not a placeholder description.

Functional requirement: player-facing audio sliders to bring SFX and music up or down individually. Also wanted: automatic audio pre-normalization and a check that catches when a scene's audio levels are too loud, so the GM/players don't have to manually ride volume.

**Named as the first of three in-scene UI elements in a follow-up message** (the other two are the character portrait frames — see in-scene-character-portrait-frames — and the personal comm device, see terminal-login-landing-page): a bar along the top or bottom of the scene, present for every player, carrying common actions and direct access to rolling the player's own character rolls, specifically 'so that any improvisation is possible' without breaking flow to dig through sheets. The GM's variant is explicitly bigger in scope than just campaign-organization controls: access to everything needed to run prepared material *or* improvise a scene on the fly, plus a **timestamped log** recording what actually happened as it happens. That log is a live-authored counterpart to chat-log-knowledge-base's post-hoc chat-scrape approach — the same 'durable record of what was actually played, not just planned' goal, captured proactively by the GM through this panel rather than reconstructed afterward.
sourceContext: User planning message, 2026-08-22 — large worldbuilding/tooling brain-dump. Elaborated further in a later planning message the same day, part of a multi-part rant about in-scene UI that also produced in-scene-character-portrait-frames and expanded terminal-login-landing-page.
